verdict: Estée Lauder's sales rose 7% to $3.7B with growth in nearly every product category and every region, and profit jumped five-fold as margins widened and restructuring charges fell — so it raised its full-year outlook.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Net sales of $3.7B, vs $3.5B a year ago; organic sales (excluding currency moves) rose 6%

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $0.13 a year ago; adjusted diluted EPS was $0.72

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: Up from 73.4% a year ago, helped by cost savings, pricing and sales leverage

segments.name: Skin Care
segments.note: Creams, serums and other skin products (La Mer, Estée Lauder and others) — the biggest category. Reported sales were $1,651M before the $1M restructuring-related returns charge absorbed here (see footer note).

segments.name: Makeup
segments.note: Cosmetics such as foundation and lipstick (MAC, Estée Lauder, Too Faced and others).

segments.name: Fragrance
segments.note: Perfumes and scented products — the fastest-growing category this quarter, up 19%.

segments.name: Hair Care
segments.note: Shampoo, treatments and styling products (Aveda, Bumble and bumble) — roughly flat.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Smaller product lines that do not fit the four main categories.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Advertising, store and counter staff, and running the company — up 3%, as higher consumer-facing investment was partly offset by savings from the Profit Recovery and Growth Plan.

opex.name: Restructuring and other charges
opex.note: Charges tied to the company's restructuring program — down from $89M a year ago.

takeaways.title: Growth in nearly everything, everywhere
takeaways.text: Net sales rose 7% to $3,715M (6% organic). Fragrance led the categories, up 19% to $861M, and every region grew on a reported basis — Mainland China sales rose 15% to $614M and Asia Pacific 9% to $952M. Management raised its fiscal 2027 outlook for sales, margin and EPS.

takeaways.title: Margins did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Gross margin widened to 75.7% from 73.4% on savings from the Profit Recovery and Growth Plan, pricing and sales leverage, and operating margin jumped to 11.0% from 4.9%. Net earnings rose to $233M from $47M, also helped by the tax rate falling to 32.5% from 56.9%.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS is a bit higher than GAAP
takeaways.text: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.72 vs $0.64 reported. The gap is mainly $41M of returns charges tied to the restructuring program, which the company excludes from its adjusted operating income of $449M (vs $408M as reported); restructuring and other charges in operating expenses were $40M, down from $89M a year ago.

oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges of $40M sit in operating expenses (down from $89M a year ago), tied to the restructuring program within the Profit Recovery and Growth Plan.

A further $41M of returns charges associated with restructuring and other activities is excluded from the company's category and regional operating results — adjusted operating income was $449M vs $408M as reported — and net sales include a $1M returns charge on the same program.
otherDetail: Other expense of $63M, net: $83M of interest expense and $5M of other pension-benefit cost, partly offset by $25M of interest income and investment income.
footerNote: Product-category sales sum to $3,716M before a $1M returns charge associated with restructuring and other activities; that $1M is absorbed in Skin Care, the largest category, so the segments sum to reported net sales of $3,715M.
